head: claude/mi176-alpaca-coverage-quantity-20260908
title: Alpaca: grade protective coverage as a QUANTITY, not just sides (detection only)
body:
## The real-money answer first

**`alpaca_live` was NOT exposed at the read — and it was FLAT, not covered. Those are different facts.**

Measured `2026-09-08T02:17:10Z` via `/api/diag/alpaca_open_orders`, direct Caddy read (exit 0):

| account | class | read_state | positions_state | positions | orders | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`alpaca_live`** | **real_money** | `orders_read` | `positions_read` | **0** | **0** | **flat — empty denominator** |
| `alpaca_paper` | paper | `orders_read` | `positions_read` | 8 | 16 | 8/8 at 1.00 stop coverage |
| `alpaca_portfolio` | paper | `orders_read` | `positions_read` | 7 | 14 | 6 at 1.00, **TLT 16/72** |
| `alpaca_options_paper` | paper | `orders_read` | `positions_read` | 0 | 0 | flat |

All four declared Alpaca accounts read cleanly on **both** sub-reads, so every absence above is **measured**, not a failed look. There were four declared accounts, not three — `alpaca_options_paper` is the fourth.

`alpaca_live` holds no position, so it has **no denominator to cover**. It must not be reported as "fully protected". It runs the same client code and trades TLT — the same symbol carrying the finding below — so it inherits the defect the moment it opens a position.

**Journal cross-check** (trades ids 4546–5545, the most recent 1000; oldest open row is 5209, clearing the window's lower bound by 663 ids): 13 open Alpaca rows — `alpaca_portfolio` 7, `alpaca_paper` 6, **`alpaca_live` zero**. Venue and journal agree.

## The paper finding, and who owns the naked shares

`alpaca_portfolio`/TLT is a **72-share short carrying a resting stop for 16 shares — 56 unprotected**.

The journal attributes it exactly: trades **5266** (16 shares, opened 08-31) and **5414** (56 shares, opened 09-03) share the one netted position, and only 5266's bracket rests. **Trade 5414 is entirely naked while declaring `stop_loss` 82.32875.**

**Positive control:** the same probe over the same read graded the other 14 open positions at exactly 1.00. The single finding is the probe discriminating, not the probe being blind.

## Why it was invisible

This is the **quantity half of `BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED`**, for the one venue that never got it. That row is filed **resolved**: the sides half landed everywhere, and the quantity half landed on IB (`IBClient.protection_coverage`) and Bybit (`_bybit_position_protection` `covered_qty`). Alpaca kept a boolean, and `_check_broker_naked_equity_positions` passed `stop_qty=None` under the literal comment `# Alpaca grades sides, not qty`. **The parent row's resolved status is what hid that for 23 days.**

Alpaca nets per symbol per account: N journal trades share ONE broker position sized to their SUM, while each bracket is sized to its OWN qty. One surviving bracket made the whole netted position read protected.

## What this ships — DETECTION ONLY

`AlpacaClient.protection_coverage` returns `{size, side, stop_qty, target_qty, legs, unknown_qty_legs, source}` — the **same vocabulary IB and Bybit already use**, not a fourth.

- A leg counts only if it **reduces** the graded position. Alpaca has no hedge mode, so the reducing side is a function of the position side; without that filter a resting same-side **entry** order counts as protection.
- An unreadable leg qty/type/side, or an unreadable position side, makes coverage **ungradeable** — never zero and never full. *We did not look* stays its own state, mirroring the IB and Bybit refusals to guess.
- A non-positive or NaN leg qty is ungradeable rather than `abs()`-ed — `abs()` launders a negative into real coverage and manufactures protection that does not rest. **Caught by its own test, not by inspection.**
- `stop_limit` counts as a **stop**, never a target — a limit-first test manufactures target coverage, strictly worse than the bug being fixed.

**Nothing is re-armed off the new grade.** The re-arm decision still reads `protection_state` byte-identically. Binding coverage to the repair path is a separate Tier-2 decision — `BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG` is what automatic remediation of this class did last time.

## Tier-2 — why this is not self-landing

`.github/pr-landing/{slug}.json` declares `tier: 2`, `landing: hold`, and no automerge request file is armed. Two runtime effects, neither of which places, cancels or modifies an order:

1. **One** additional account-wide `positions()` read per **account** per sweep, memoized — deliberately not one per position per tick. This sweep runs on every tick, and an unbounded per-row broker call on the live tick is the shape of both June 2026 wedges.
2. A new **CRITICAL** page `alpaca_partial_stop_coverage`, on the shared durable 6h/(account,symbol) cooldown with the **uncovered quantity as its severity**, so a worsening breaks the window while a persisting or improving condition stays suppressed. It **will** fire on merge for the standing TLT condition — that is the finding, not a regression.

## Verification

- 23 new assertions in `tests/test_alpaca_protection_coverage_quantity.py`, fixtures taken from the live reading above.
- 98 adjacent existing tests pass (`test_alpaca_protection_two_sided`, `test_alpaca_naked_rearm`, `test_naked_position_autoprotect`, `test_target_naked_cooldown_is_durable`, `test_protection_price`).
- `run_guards.py --base main`: **PASS 70 · FAIL 0**.
- The new code path was replayed against the real venue payload and reproduces exactly one finding — the TLT partial — and nothing spurious.

⚠️ **A green harness cannot reach the live monitor tick.** This is deployed, not proven; `OI-20260908-ALPACA-QUANTITY-COVERAGE-SHIPPED-AND-A-56-SHARE-NAKED-POSITION-IS-STANDING` carries both that and the standing naked position.

## Coordination board

**Could not claim.** Issue #6927 is at GitHub's hard 2500-comment cap — writes 403 and reads return a board frozen at 2026-09-07T11:28:17Z. The mandatory START claim could not be posted; known and parked, not skipped by choice.

## Open decision for the operator

Should the quantity grade **bind** the Alpaca re-arm/top-up path as Bybit's does — the Alpaca analogue of `BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_MODE`, staged per account with an empty allowlist meaning NONE? Until then a partially-covered Alpaca position is detected and pages, and is **not** repaired. Separately, the standing 56 naked shares on trade 5414 need a disposition.
